description: This Mendeley Data workbook reports seventeen preprocessed microscale walkability indicators for fifty-nine European central urban areas in twenty-six countries. GeoCHOROS and collaborators derived the indicators from street observation and GIS analysis to describe pedestrian environments. The article lists centre-level aggregated tabular data, and the current repository version 2 exposes one XLSX file under CC BY 4.0. Its scope is central areas selected for this study, not all neighbourhoods in the cities or a direct measure of individual walking trips. Observation protocol, indicator definitions and varying central-area boundaries are limitations when comparing cities or transferring values to a pedestrian simulation. A reviewer-assessed use is setting urban-form inputs or screening public-space interventions for active-mobility models. data-openstreetmap is a related geographic base, but no street-level reconciliation was tested. A separate Mendeley release holds fifty-metre GIS grids with a different licence, and a public code repository holds the web interface. No workbook was downloaded.
